Subject: Publishable privacy takeaways for Hosted API — plain language draft

Hi all,

Following up from last week's call with Acme — they asked for a single-screen, sales-friendly explanation of how data moves and what subprocessors we use for the Hosted API (console card + help center link). 

We tried to keep the attached short blurb concise, but Acme flagged two things: (1) the subprocessor language is too technical for non-legal buyers, and (2) the transfer/ residency sentence feels like it could be misread by security teams.

Can Legal/Product help with two things:
- a 1-line option (short card) + a 2–3 sentence companion (help center) in plain language;
- a constrained set of terms we can use in sales collateral so we don't accidentally imply broader data access than we provide (e.g., "no human access" vs "limited ops access").

Attached: hosted_api_privacy_snippet_v1.md (our draft) and a CSV export of current subprocessors. I tried a one-liner below as a starting point.

One-line (starter): "Your data stays encrypted and is processed by Redwood Inference and select cloud partners only for inference; see our subprocessor map for details."

Thanks — Ben

--

Ben — thanks for the concise draft and for sharing Acme's feedback. I read the attachments and pulled a few high-level notes: 

- Happy to create a two-tier set: (A) 1-line card for the console and sales one-pager, (B) 2–3 sentence help center blurb that preserves legal accuracy.
- "Your data stays encrypted" is fine but we should avoid definitive language like "no human access" unless we qualify it ("no routine human access except for approved, logged support operations").
- For subprocessors, we should standardize phrasing: "We use a limited set of subprocessors (cloud infra, logging, metrics). See current list." That avoids implying permanence — good for procurement review.

Inline edits to your one-liner (first pass):
"Redwood processes requests using encryption in transit and at rest. We process data in support of providing inference; only approved subprocessors (cloud infrastructure and monitoring providers) may process data on our behalf — see the subprocessor map for locations and roles."

A couple of asks for Acme (copying them transparently):
- Can you confirm whether you need guaranteed residency for inference or only for stored artifacts/backups? That changes the wording re: residency controls.
- Any specific controls you need called out (e.g., customer-managed keys, HSM)?

Jonas — I expect you can help with the technical accuracy on caching, KV retention and how to phrase "inference only" vs "data retention".

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Thanks Laura — below are a few clarifications and two short wording proposals (1-line + help blurb). I tried to favor clarity over legalese while leaving accuracy intact.

Tech clarifications (can be cited in the help text):
- Inference path: we process request payloads in memory on GPU; we do not persist request content to long-term storage by default.
- Caching/KV: customers may enable KV caching; if enabled, cached keys are stored per-customer and TTLs are configurable.
- Subprocessors: current set includes primary cloud provider (managed compute), object storage for artifacts, monitoring/logging vendors. We rotate/add subprocessors quarterly — link to live map is best.

Wording A — 1-line console card (very short):
"Redwood processes API requests for inference using encryption; only Redwood and a short list of approved cloud partners process your data — see our live subprocessor map for details."

Wording B — 2–3 sentence help-center blurb (companion):
"When you call the Hosted API, request data is processed in memory for inference and is encrypted in transit and at rest. Redwood and a limited set of approved subprocessors (cloud compute, storage, monitoring) process data only to provide the service; cached data is subject to customer-configurable retention. See the subprocessor map and residency controls for details and locations."

If Acme needs guaranteed residency for inference (all compute kept in a region), that's a product capability we can commit to under Dedicated / Private offerings but not for standard Hosted; we should be explicit about that choice in the copy.

Suggested next step: Laura/Legal to approve the help blurb, then we push the 1-line to the console card and link to the help center detailed blurb and live subprocessor map. I can also add a short FAQ entry clarifying KV caching behavior.

-Jonas

Acme — to answer your residency question: for Hosted API we can’t guarantee inference compute residency on the standard plan; we can offer region-specific deployments on Dedicated or Private. If your requirement is only for backups/artifacts, we can document retention/residency controls in the help center and offer customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
